text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Does the child have any history of frequent infections, fever, or fatigue, and have any recent medications, such as aspirin or NSAIDs, been administered?

speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted the symptoms of frequent epistaxis, mucous membrane bleeding, and diffuse petechiae, but I will disregard the unrelated text regarding pneumonia. To narrow down the cause, has the child experienced any recent viral illnesses, and have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes or an enlarged spleen or liver?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given the presentation of petechiae and mucosal bleeding, I need to rule out bone marrow involvement or severe platelet destruction. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Platform_Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells. Coagulation Profile: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count and coagulation profile, combined with the specific deficiency in GPIIb/IIIa receptors, confirm a diagnosis of Glanzmann thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
